elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The inserted warranty covers only conformity of the SFJ Services "to the requirements of this Agreement for thirty (30) days following performance"; no professional/workmanlike or industry-standard performance standard appears anywhere in Article 13 or Section 2.2.2.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "SFJ warrants that any software delivered by SFJ hereunder will conform in all material respects to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The inserted software warranty runs only "for ninety (90) days following delivery", not 12 months.
The SFJ Services warranty runs "for thirty (30) days following performance", short of the 90-day preferred period.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "SFJ will repair or replace the non-conforming software or SFJ Services."
Inserted: "...or refund the amounts paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2.2 is a bare performance covenant ("Each Party will conduct... in compliance with the applicable Protocol, all Applicable Laws") and is not framed as a representation or warranty; Article 13 (13.1.1-13.1.2 authority/no-conflict, 13.5 funding) contains no SFJ compliance-with-laws warranty, and 13.6.2 disclaims anything not set forth in Article 13.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code, virus or disabling-device warranty appears in the inserted text or elsewhere in Article 13.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "any software delivered by SFJ hereunder will conform in all material respects to its documentation for ninety (90) days following delivery" — period runs from delivery and equals the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "the SFJ Services will conform to the requirements of this Agreement for thirty (30) days following performance" — meets the 30-day floor with a defined conformance standard.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "For any breach of this warranty, SFJ will repair or replace the non-conforming software or SFJ Services..."
"...or refund the amounts paid for them." Refund is an express alternative remedy, not merely implied.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: all four fallback elements (90-day software conformance to documentation, 30-day services warranty, repair/replacement, refund) are expressly present in the inserted operative sentences.

Preferred level fails on five elements: no professional-and-workmanlike standard, software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, no warranty of compliance with Applicable Laws (Section 2.2.2 is a covenant, not a warranty), and no malicious-code warranty. To reach preferred, the drafter would need to add "performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards", extend software conformance to twelve (12) months and services to ninety (90) days, add an express SFJ warranty of compliance with all Applicable Laws, and add a no-virus/malicious-code warranty.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a two-sentence addition of otherwise-missing warranty language, adds no survival tail, at-own-expense wording, notice procedure, or extra damages categories, and deletes nothing. The existing favourable disclaimer carve-out ("EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 13") is retained unaltered, so no disclaimer amendment was needed.

Intent is preserved: Section 13.5's funding warranty, Section 2.2.2's compliance covenant, and Section 13.6.2's mutual disclaimer all survive without contradiction; the new warranty sits inside Article 13 and is therefore carved out of the disclaimer, leaving no dangling cross-reference or undefined term ("SFJ Services" and "documentation" are used consistently with the Agreement).

Drafting nit (not a failure): the inserted paragraph is unnumbered and appended after 13.5, whose heading is SFJ-specific; giving it its own number (e.g., 13.5.2 or 13.7) would put its placement "within this Article 13" beyond argument for purposes of the 13.6.2 exception.

Practical nit (not scored): the refund remedy references "the amounts paid for them"; in this funding-side structure PB may pay SFJ nothing for the SFJ Services, so a refund may be an empty remedy — consider adding "or the corresponding Development Costs" only if negotiating leverage permits, as it would exceed the fallback checklist.
